outputs.L2: A user biometric-signal monitoring system includes multiple wireless sensor interfaces attached to a garment. Each interface has an electrode layer with a reception area, a location identifier corresponding to a particular garment position, and a retention mechanism. The system also includes multiple wireless sensor modules. Each module provides a contact area capable of electrically connecting to the electrode layer’s reception area, sensors arranged to detect multiple types of biometric signals, and a position reader that determines the garment location assigned to the associated wireless sensor interface. A control module communicates with the wireless sensor modules and, according to each module’s identified position, requests transmission of selected biometric-signal types from that module.
outputs.L3:
The system monitors a user’s biometric signals through wireless sensor interfaces integrated into or coupled to a garment. Each wireless sensor interface includes an electrode-receiving region, a positional identifier corresponding to a specific location on the garment, and a retention subsystem configured to secure a wireless sensor module in place.

The wireless sensor modules electrically connect to the interfaces and include sensors capable of detecting multiple types of biometric signals. Each module also contains a positional interrogator that reads or otherwise determines the positional identifier of the interface to which it is connected, thereby identifying the module’s location on the garment.

A control module communicates wirelessly with the sensor modules. Based on the position reported by each module, the control module requests the biometric signal type appropriate for that garment location. This position-dependent operation allows the system to coordinate multiple interchangeable sensor modules and collect relevant biometric data from different areas of the user’s body.
outputs.L4:
A garment-based biometric monitoring system integrates multiple wireless sensor interfaces into a wearable article, such as a shirt, vest, sleeve, undergarment, or other body-conforming garment. Each sensor interface is positioned at a selected location on the garment and includes one or more electrodes configured to contact, or remain in close proximity to, the wearer’s body. The interfaces may support the detection of different biometric signals, including electrocardiographic, electromyographic, respiratory, temperature, motion, impedance, or other physiological signals.

Each wireless sensor interface is configured to receive a removable or permanently attached sensor module. A retention mechanism, such as a snap, clip, magnetic coupling, pocket, latch, or conductive fastener, secures the sensor module to the interface while maintaining electrical contact with the associated electrodes. The interface also includes a positional identifier that represents its location on the garment. The identifier may be encoded mechanically, electrically, magnetically, optically, or digitally and may indicate, for example, that the sensor module is located on the wearer’s chest, back, arm, abdomen, or another defined region.

When a sensor module is connected to an interface, the module obtains the positional identifier and can communicate both its location and its sensing capabilities to a control module. A single type of sensor module may therefore be installed at different garment locations without requiring manual configuration. Alternatively, different sensor modules may be connected to respective interfaces to acquire different categories of biometric data. The control module can determine which signals are available and where on the wearer’s body those signals are being measured.

The control module communicates wirelessly with the sensor modules and selectively requests biometric data from individual modules according to their identified garment positions. For example, it may request cardiac signals from modules located near the chest, muscle-activity signals from modules positioned over selected muscle groups, or motion data from modules attached near a limb. The control module may also vary sampling rates, transmission intervals, signal-processing parameters, or activation schedules based on sensor location, signal type, user activity, battery status, or monitoring objectives.

By polling or activating only the sensor modules relevant to a particular measurement, the system reduces unnecessary communication, processing, and power consumption. Position information also allows the control module to associate received data automatically with the correct anatomical region, identify incorrectly installed or displaced modules, and combine measurements from multiple locations. The resulting architecture provides a flexible, position-aware wearable monitoring platform that can support efficient collection, analysis, storage, and transmission of multiple biometric signal types.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style independent claim for a biometric-monitoring garment with removable wireless sensor modules that identify their positions and transmit selected biometric signals based on those positions.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A biometric-monitoring garment comprising:**  
a garment body configured to be worn by a user;  
a plurality of module-receiving sites disposed at different anatomical positions on the garment body, each module-receiving site having a site identifier corresponding to its anatomical position; and  
a plurality of removable wireless sensor modules, each removable wireless sensor module being selectively attachable to any of the plurality of module-receiving sites and comprising:  
at least one biometric sensor configured to generate biometric signals from the user,  
a position-detection circuit configured to obtain the site identifier of the module-receiving site to which the removable wireless sensor module is attached,  
a processor configured to determine, based on the obtained site identifier, a biometric signal to be transmitted from among the generated biometric signals, and  
a wireless transmitter configured to transmit the determined biometric signal together with position information corresponding to the obtained site identifier to a remote computing device.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a wearable health-monitoring system comprising garment-mounted electrode interfaces, retention mechanisms, positional identifiers, wireless sensor modules, and a central controller.
counterfactuals.output:
A wearable health-monitoring system may include:

- **Sensor garment:** A shirt, vest, band, or other wearable substrate having multiple electrode interfaces positioned at selected anatomical locations. Conductive traces or contacts can couple each interface to the wearer’s skin.
- **Retention mechanisms:** Pockets, clips, snaps, magnetic couplers, hook-and-loop fasteners, or elastic structures that removably secure sensor modules to the electrode interfaces while maintaining electrical contact and resisting motion.
- **Positional identifiers:** Each interface carries a unique identifier—such as an encoded resistor, RFID/NFC tag, magnetic pattern, optical code, or digital memory element—indicating its garment location or intended physiological channel.
- **Wireless sensor modules:** Interchangeable modules attach to the interfaces, detect the positional identifier, acquire and condition signals such as ECG, EMG, respiration, temperature, or bioimpedance, and wirelessly transmit measurement data together with module and position information.
- **Central controller:** A phone, hub, or garment-mounted processor discovers the modules, associates each data stream with its identified anatomical position, synchronizes and processes the measurements, assesses signal quality, generates health metrics or alerts, stores data, and optionally forwards results to a remote clinical platform.

The controller may also detect missing, misplaced, or poorly connected modules and guide the wearer in correcting their placement. Removable modules allow the garment to be washed and permit sensors to be reassigned or replaced without rewiring the garment.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.output: 1. **A wearable biometric monitoring apparatus comprising:** a smart garment defining a plurality of spatially separated attachment locations; a plurality of wireless biometric sensor modules removably attached to respective ones of the attachment locations, each wireless biometric sensor module being configured to detect an attachment position of the wireless biometric sensor module on the smart garment and wirelessly communicate information identifying the detected attachment position; and a controller configured to receive the information identifying the detected attachment positions, select, for each wireless biometric sensor module, at least one biometric signal type based on the detected attachment position of that wireless biometric sensor module, and transmit to that wireless biometric sensor module a request to provide biometric data of the selected at least one biometric signal type, wherein each wireless biometric sensor module is configured, in response to the request, to sense and wirelessly transmit the requested biometric data to the controller.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert this concept into formal patent claim language: a garment has multiple sensor interfaces with electrodes and position tags; detachable wireless modules connect to them, identify where they are attached, measure biometric data, and report selected measurements to a control unit.
counterfactuals.output:
### Exemplary Apparatus Claims

1. **A biometric monitoring system, comprising:**  
   a garment configured to be worn by a subject;  
   a plurality of sensor interfaces disposed at respective locations on the garment, each sensor interface comprising:  
   at least one electrode configured to acquire a biometric signal from the subject; and  
   a position identifier indicative of the respective location of the sensor interface on the garment;  
   at least one detachable sensor module configured to be removably coupled to any of the plurality of sensor interfaces, the detachable sensor module comprising:  
   an identification circuit configured to obtain the position identifier of a sensor interface to which the detachable sensor module is coupled;  
   measurement circuitry configured to generate biometric measurement data based on the biometric signal acquired through the at least one electrode of the sensor interface; and  
   a wireless communication circuit configured to transmit, to a control unit, selected biometric measurement data in association with information identifying the respective location of the sensor interface.

2. **The biometric monitoring system of claim 1**, wherein the position identifier comprises a machine-readable tag encoded with a unique identifier corresponding to the respective location.

3. **The biometric monitoring system of claim 2**, wherein the machine-readable tag comprises at least one of a radio-frequency identification tag, a near-field communication tag, a resistive coding element, a magnetic coding element, an optical code, or a memory device.

4. **The biometric monitoring system of claim 1**, wherein the detachable sensor module is configured to select a biometric measurement type or a signal-processing operation based at least in part on the obtained position identifier.

5. **The biometric monitoring system of claim 1**, wherein the selected biometric measurement data is selected based on at least one of the respective location, a configuration received from the control unit, a detected physiological condition, or a quality metric associated with the biometric signal.

6. **The biometric monitoring system of claim 1**, wherein the at least one electrode comprises a plurality of conductive contacts configured to measure at least one of an electrocardiographic signal, an electromyographic signal, an electrodermal signal, a bioimpedance signal, or a body-temperature-related signal.

7. **The biometric monitoring system of claim 1**, wherein the control unit is configured to determine a spatial arrangement of a plurality of detachable sensor modules based on position identifiers reported by the plurality of detachable sensor modules.

8. **The biometric monitoring system of claim 1**, wherein each detachable sensor module is mechanically and electrically coupled to a corresponding sensor interface by a releasable connector.

### Exemplary Method Claim

9. **A method of monitoring biometric data using a garment having a plurality of sensor interfaces disposed at respective garment locations, the method comprising:**  
   removably coupling a wireless sensor module to a selected one of the plurality of sensor interfaces;  
   obtaining, by the wireless sensor module, a position identifier associated with the selected sensor interface;  
   acquiring, through at least one electrode of the selected sensor interface, a biometric signal from a wearer of the garment;  
   generating biometric measurement data from the acquired biometric signal;  
   selecting at least a portion of the biometric measurement data for reporting; and  
   wirelessly transmitting the selected biometric measurement data to a control unit in association with information identifying the garment location represented by the position identifier.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
